facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of a rapidly enlarging left breast mass
no history of pain, trauma, fever, anorexia, or weight loss
the left breast had a 20 cm × 20 cm well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump
the right breast was normal
the mass was not fixed to skin or underlying muscle
the overlying skin was tense and shiny with prominent superficial veins
no nipple discharge and no axillary lymphadenopathy
routine hematological and biochemical tests, including ESR, were within normal limits
a chest radiograph was normal
ultrasonography of the left breast revealed a heterogeneous parenchymal pattern suggestive of fibroadenoma
fine-needle aspiration cytology of the lump showed pathology suggesting fibroadenoma
she was premenarcheal

concepts.why: The patient's ultrasonography and fine-needle aspiration cytology results suggest fibroadenoma, which is consistent with the physical examination findings of a well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump.

The patient's physical examination findings of a well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump could also be consistent with a breast cyst, although the ultrasonography and fine-needle aspiration cytology results suggest fibroadenoma.
The patient's ultrasonography and fine-needle aspiration cytology results suggest a benign breast tumor, which is consistent with the diagnosis of fibroadenoma.
The patient's age and ultrasonography and fine-needle aspiration cytology results suggest juvenile fibroadenoma, which is a type of benign breast tumor that occurs in young girls.
